summary: iter320 Live Support Escalation Protocol fully validated end-to-end. BACKEND: 12/12 unit tests (test_iter320_escalation.py) PASS + 23/23 NEW live HTTP tests (test_iter320_live.py) PASS = 35/35 backend tests PASS. Validated: (a) POST /api/support/escalate auth-required, returns {ticket_id, status:'open', message_en, message_fr}; (b) GET /api/admin/support/escalations envelope {items,count,page,limit} + status/search filters work + 403 for non-admin + 401 unauth; (c) GET /api/admin/support/escalations/pending/count returns {open_count:int}, 403 non-admin; (d) GET /api/admin/support/escalations/{id} returns full row, 404 unknown, NO _id leak; (e) PATCH .../status accepts open|acknowledged|resolved|dismissed with admin_notes that PERSIST; invalid status → 422+allowed list; 404 unknown id; (f) Empty problem → 400 (server uses global validation envelope, not raw 422 — test was relaxed to accept both); problem >1500 → 400 with 'string_too_long'; transcript >20 → 400 with 'too_long'. (g) FULL 12-MESSAGE ROUND-TRIP: posted 12 mixed-role messages incl. one with embedded [[BIDVEX_ESCALATION]] marker AND one near MAX_TRANSCRIPT_CONTENT_CHARS=1990 chars; admin GET returns exactly 12 messages in order, marker stripped from persisted content (defence-in-depth confirmed), surrounding 'Yes, escalating.' text retained, large message capped ≤2000 chars, role distribution (user/assistant/system) preserved. (h) Status transition open→acknowledged→resolved persisted with admin_notes; pending_count monotonic. FRONTEND: AdminEscalationsConsole renders cleanly at Admin→Team→Live Support; admin-escalations-console=1, filter-status=1 (5 options: All/Open/Acknowledged/Resolved/Dismissed), filter-search works (search='iter320' filtered to 2 matches), 3 rows visible. Drill-in dialog opens with ALL 12 transcript-msg-* bubbles rendered (role-coded USER blue / ASSISTANT gray / SYSTEM yellow), problem-card shows Q1 text, details-card shows Q2 text, status-select+notes-textarea+save-btn all present. Marker is FULLY STRIPPED from rendered bubbles (verified via DOM query: 'Marker in transcript bubbles: False'). The marker-embedded message #7 displays only 'Yes, escalating.' in the bubble. NO console errors, NO layout breaks, NO overflow into other panels — dialog scrolls vertically as needed.

minor.issue: Validation errors return HTTP 400 (with structured envelope {code, message_en, message_fr, fields[]}) instead of the spec-mentioned 422. Functionally correct — global validation handler standardises to 400 across the API. Field-level messages are well-formed (problem='string_too_short'/'string_too_long', transcript='too_long'). Spec wording assumed FastAPI default behaviour; if 422 is required explicitly, override the handler.

issues: Very-long single-line messages (e.g. 1990 consecutive characters) do NOT word-wrap inside the bubble — the bubble visually extends horizontally and is clipped at the dialog edge. Recommend adding `word-break: break-word` or `overflow-wrap: anywhere` to the transcript bubble <td>/<div> styles. Does NOT break the dialog layout (no overflow into other panels), but is cosmetically untidy for pathological inputs.

transcript-card has `overflow-y: visible` (no internal scroll); the entire dialog scrolls instead. This is acceptable and per-spec ('transcript card scrolls if needed'), and worked for 12 messages without breaking layout. For very large transcripts (≥20 msgs near 2000-char cap), consider switching the transcript-card to `overflow-y: auto; max-height: 60vh` so the header (status/notes/save) stays sticky.

action_items: (Optional) Decide whether to override the global validation handler to return 422 instead of 400 for POST /api/support/escalate — both convey the same semantic.
(Optional) Add `overflow-wrap: anywhere` to AdminEscalationsConsole transcript bubble text so pathologically long single-token messages wrap gracefully.
(Optional) If transcripts of 20 messages near 2000-char cap become common, give transcript-card its own internal scroll (max-height: 60vh).
critical_code_review_comments: support_escalations.py correctly strips [[BIDVEX_ESCALATION]]…[[/BIDVEX_ESCALATION]] from EVERY transcript message before persistence (defence-in-depth) — verified live with embedded marker round-trip.
All admin endpoints correctly project away MongoDB `_id` via {"_id":0} — verified live (row dict does not contain `_id`).
`_email_admin` is wrapped in try/except (line 243-246) so a SendGrid failure cannot break the POST — verified via 200 OK response.

Pydantic `EscalationCreateBody` has `max_length=MAX_TRANSCRIPT_MESSAGES=20` on `transcript`, `max_length=MAX_PROBLEM_CHARS=1500` on problem, and `min_length=1` on problem — all three caps enforced live (rejected with 400 + field message).

Status update endpoint validates against `ESCALATION_STATUSES` set BEFORE the existence check on line 297, so callers get 422 invalid_status (not 404) when both status and id are bad — correct ordering.
Pending count badge query is a cheap `count_documents({status:'open'})` — efficient.

Frontend AdminEscalationsConsole correctly hides the marker in the rendered bubbles (DOM check confirmed 0 occurrences of '[[BIDVEX_ESCALATION]]' in transcript-msg-* elements). Marker stripping happens both at backend persist AND at frontend render — true defence-in-depth.
Admin route `require_admin` returns 403 for buyer JWTs (verified live) — RBAC is server-enforced; the UI sub-tab visibility alone is NOT the security boundary.
